stories.title: Flintshire Council tip charges meant to raise £500,000 brought less than £17,000
stories.summary: Charges for dumping DIY waste and trade waste at Flintshire’s household recycling centres were meant to raise £500,000 a year. They brought in £16,438 last year, the council’s own auditors have found. The council’s budget for 2024/25 included £300,000 a year from charging residents to take DIY and building waste to its tips. stories.title: Minimum price of alcohol in Wales rises from 50p to 65p a unit
stories.summary: From today, the minimum price of a unit of alcohol in Wales rises from 50p to 65p, the first increase since minimum pricing was introduced in March 2020. stories.title: Grants of up to £300,000 on offer for property and business owners in seven Flintshire towns
stories.summary: Shop, property and business owners in seven Flintshire towns can apply for grants of up to £300,000 to improve buildings, fill empty units and grow their businesses. Buckley, Connah’s Quay, Flint, Holywell, Mold, Queensferry and Shotton are the towns covered by Flintshire County Council’s new THRIVE Programme. stories.title: More than £1bn in benefits goes unclaimed in Wales every year, Welsh Government says
stories.summary: More than £1bn in benefits goes unclaimed in Wales every year, according to the Welsh Government, which is urging people to get a free benefit check before winter. stories.title: Review to examine how NHS waiting times in Wales have affected people’s health
stories.summary: The Health Foundation will carry out an independent review of NHS performance in Wales, the Welsh Government has confirmed.
